title: Enhanced Magnetocaloric Properties of the (MnNi)<sub>0.6</sub>Si<sub>0.62</sub>(FeCo)<sub>0.4</sub>Ge<sub>0.38</sub> High-Entropy Alloy Obtained by Co Substitution.

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic high-entropy alloy based on Mn, Ni, Si, Fe, Co and Ge with nominal composition (MnNi)0.6Si0.62(FeCo)0.4Ge0.38
recollection.intervention: Partial substitution of Fe by Co carried out via arc-melting followed by homogenization anneal, with systematic variation of the Co content to tune magnetic interactions
recollection.structure: Hexagonal (Ni2In-type) crystal structure with evidence of two coexisting phases near the magnetic transition (one richer in Co, one richer in Fe)
recollection.mechanism: Co substitution strengthens ferromagnetic exchange and sharpens a coupled magnetostructural transition, leading to a first-order metamagnetic change at a tunable temperature
recollection.results: Best sample (≈10 at.% extra Co) exhibits a peak magnetic entropy change –ΔSm ≈3.4 J kg–1 K–1 under a 5 T field change near 290 K, with a refrigerant capacity of ≈125 J kg–1 and reduced thermal hysteresis (≈1.5 K) compared to the parent alloy

score.note: The recollection correctly mentions arc melting, annealing, systematic Co variation, the Ni2In-type hexagonal phase, and a coupled magnetostructural transition. However, it incorrectly says Co substitutes for Fe rather than Ni, invents Co-rich/Fe-rich phase coexistence, and misstates the mechanism: Co stabilizes the hexagonal austenite through stronger Mn–Mn covalent bonding and lowers transition temperatures, while excessive Co removes first-order coupling. The reported entropy change and hysteresis are far from the actual values (peak −ΔSM up to 48.5 J kg−1 K−1 and hysteresis around 20 K for the strongest sample).
